text:
anya: FYI, nightly evals show a sudden spike for redwood-1b-quant on prompt-set `qcr-small` — failures jumped from ~3% to 23% at 03:00 UTC :eyes:

eval-bot: nightly-run 1792001234 redwood-1b-quant qcr-small: 46/200 prompts failed, median BLEU drop 0.34

anya: failing gens look like tiny tokenization shifts, e.g. expected `don't` -> got `don’ t` (curly apostrophe + extra space) on multiple prompts. attaching one example that used to pass:

sam: can you paste the raw generation / tokenized representation?

anya: sure:
```
prompt: What's the policy on student loan forgiveness?
expected: We do not have a blanket student loan forgiveness policy.
actual: We don’t  have a blanket student loan forgiveness policy.
tokenized_expected: ["We", "do", "n't", "have", ...]
tokenized_actual: ["We", "don’", "t", "have", ...]
```

miguel: hmm that looks like a tokenizer normalization change (ASCII apostrophe vs right single quotation mark). Haven't seen this randomly flip before. Any infra changes in the last deploy?

tara: Docker base image for nightly runners was rebuilt last night with the new `py-base:2026-03-18` — ci pinned to `python:3.11-slim` but our base image includes a prebuilt `tokenizers` wheel. Maybe wheel got rebuilt with a different rust/tokenizer version.

leigh: +1. I just spot-checked the images on two runner nodes:
- runner-a: Python 3.11.4, tokenizers==0.13.3
- runner-b: Python 3.11.4, tokenizers==0.14.0

sam: that would do it. tokenizers 0.14 changed some unicode normalizations for apostrophes in the default pre-tokenization pipeline (PR note: handle curly quotes). If some nodes use 0.13.x and others 0.14.x you'll get non-deterministic test outcomes across the fleet.

anya: how did we end up with mixed versions? we thought the base image pinned wheels.

tara: aws AMI build pulled from the wheel cache and one builder used the cached 0.13 wheel, the other rebuilt at 0.14 due to cache miss. The image tag didn't change so runners rolled with mixed tokenizers.

miguel: repro locally by running the harness inside two different thin images:
```
docker run --rm redwood/nightly:py-base bash -lc "python -c \"import tokenizers; print(tokenizers.__version__)\""
```
I reproduced both 0.13.3 and 0.14.0 on two different local images.

sam: quick mitigation: add a tokenization roundtrip check in the harness before running quality evals. E.g. for every prompt set, run: `tok.encode(prompt).decode(tok.encode(prompt).ids)` and assert identical normalized string. If fails, mark the node unhealthy.

anya: agreed. Also pin tokenizers==0.13.3 in our base image to stop drift until we intentionally upgrade + run compatibility tests.

tara: I'll roll a patched base image with pinned wheel and push to `py-base:2026-03-19-patch1`. Will also invalidate the old AMI builder cache. ETA 45m.

eval-bot: quick check job: tokenization-roundtrip qcr-small on runner-a -> PASS (tokenizers 0.13.3)

leigh: runner-b -> FAIL (tokenizers 0.14.0) reproduces the split.

anya: patch + restart nightly scheduler after tara pushes?

tara: pushing now, kicking off a small canary run on 3 nodes.

sam: once canary passes, we should enqueue an automation task: (1) add tokenizers version check to our infra-level health probe, (2) add a unit test in eval-harness that compares tokenization outputs between pinned version and the version under test to detect semantic diffs early.

miguel: also file an issue to upstream tokenizers to document the normalization change and any migration steps. Might be important for reproducibility.

anya: can we also surface a short human-readable note in the nightly report when tokenization mismatches are detected so triage is easier?

tara: yep I'll add a tokenization-check block in the nightly summary page that lists nodes with mismatched versions / failures.

eval-bot: canary-run 1792001700: redwood-1b-quant qcr-small after patch -> 2/200 fails (baseline ~3%) — regressions gone.

anya: awesome — closing this loop. follow-ups:
- tara: AMI + image cleanup (in progress)
- sam: add harness tokenization roundtrip test (PR queued)
- miguel: file upstream tokenizers issue + doc note
- leigh: add tokenizers version check to infra health probe

anya: thanks all. lesson: binary wheels + builder cache churn can silently change our eval signal. leaving a short postmortem note in #postmortems once we finish the fixes. :party_parrot:
